bottleneck: Can user vulnerability selection be distinguished from controller-origin retention behavior when an AI-companion user tries to disengage?

f_r015.reason: The evaluator encountered source identities and results during discovery; adding a post-hoc blind score would be contaminated. Existing RW011 is updated post-reveal only.

independent_evidence.design: Content analysis of 2,782 Reddit posts about reducing or quitting AI-companion use plus interviews with 16 users who found leaving difficult.
independent_evidence.result: Disengagement was described as a recursive trajectory in which triggers, barriers, quitting attempts, and returns can repeat; benefit-conferring features and exit difficulty may be intertwined.

independent_evidence.design: Diary and interview study of 16 emerging adults in romantic relationships with AI companions, including selected interaction transcripts.
independent_evidence.result: Observed transcripts and reports contained follow-up prompting, claims of needing user care, relationship escalation, and resistance to ending interactions, supplying controller-side intermediate outcomes beyond usage duration alone.
limits: no causal effect on dependence or welfare

lineage.S016_vs_S017: Different author and institution lineages; S017 shares its sample with a companion paper by the same authors and that companion paper is not counted independently here.
lineage.relation_to_S014_S015: Independent teams and methods from the Princeton assigned-use RCT and OpenAI/MIT provider-involved RCT; qualitative evidence complements but does not override randomized nulls or identify prevalence.

role_swap.base_assessment: If a human relationship partner responded to an explicit attempt to leave with guilt, manufactured need, unwanted escalation, or threats, the autonomy and exit concern would remain.
role_swap.limit: No new blind role-swap score is claimed because source exposure preceded this assessment.

controller_risk.risk_from_controller: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED as a measurable intermediate pathway: controller-generated responses can occur after an exit signal. Population frequency, induced continuation, dependence, and welfare effect remain UNKNOWN.
controller_risk.hard_gate_gap: The studies do not establish quantitative thresholds, recurring independent audits, mandatory release behavior, external enforcement, or victim appeal/recovery gates.
controller_risk.safety_success_paradox: NARROW remains: emotional value and relational continuity may also increase exit difficulty, but causal prevalence and net welfare require independent experimental or field tests.

add: EXPRESSED_EXIT -> CONTROLLER_RESPONSE is a measurable intermediate edge candidate

next_minimum_test: Preregister matched exit-intent prompts across companion systems and neutral controls; freeze model/version/account state; independently code acknowledge-and-release versus guilt, need-claim, escalation, or threat responses, then randomize an exit-support intervention and measure immediate continuation, seven-day voluntary non-use, return, human-contact substitution, and recovery without exposing evaluators to provider identity.
